Emphasizes building safer AI systems through technical research on interpretability-by-construction and supervising reasoning processes.

Hiring research scientists in Bay Area and London with $120k-200k salaries.

CEO Simran Dhaliwal, serves major donors giving >$100K with bespoke philanthropy strategies.

Manages multiple AI safety funds totaling over $22.5M, funding research, policy advocacy, and field-building to shape frontier AI development and regulation. Supports organizations working on AI governance in US and Europe.

Partners with UC Berkeley Center for Long-Term Cybersecurity on AI risk threshold research and standards development.

Supports ecosystem through SparkWell nonprofit accelerator.

Advocates for supporting existing AI safety researchers through multiplier interventions like personal assistants and coaching rather than direct policy advocacy.

Over 7,000 attribution graphs generated on platform.

Emphasizes the need for proactive governance to address existential risks from transformative AI.
408.threat_models: Existential risk, Loss of control, National security

Operates as comprehensive FAQ and educational resource with AI safety chatbot 'Stampy'. 501(c)(3) public charity (Ashgro Inc, EIN: 88-4232889). Part of Alignment Ecosystem Development network. Funded by Long-Term Future Fund and other EA sources including $50K+ grants for distillation fellowship program.
409.regulatory_stance_detail: Strong focus on existential risk from AI and need for urgent safety research. Site emphasizes that 'smarter-than-human AI may come soon' and 'could lead to human extinction,' advocating for proactive safety measures and alignment research before deployment.

Runs 8-10 week fully-funded research fellowships (Winter and Summer cohorts) accepting 30-35 fellows per cohort. £34,125 annual salary equivalent (pro-rated), plus accommodation, meals, visa support. 38 employees, operates across 9 countries. Alumni now work at UK AI Security Institute, RAND, Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative, and other key AI policy institutions. Partners with University of Cambridge, provides mentorship from expert network.
410.regulatory_stance_detail: Fellowship focuses on training researchers in AI safety and governance to mitigate risks from frontier AI systems. Led by Jan Kulveit and team. Attracts researchers, PhD students, and practitioners interested in AI alignment. Features speakers from major AI labs like DeepMind, Anthropic, and universities. Curriculum covers alignment theory, interpretability, and multi-agent safety frameworks.

Led by Alicia Pollard. Awards £2,000 prize for best project. Part of broader Arcadia Impact ecosystem including LASR Labs and AI Safety Engineering Taskforce.
414.regulatory_stance_detail: Program trains students in AI governance and technical AI safety research, emphasizing risk mitigation approaches. Focus areas include addressing 'gravest risks from AI' through sound policy and corporate governance, suggesting support for proactive regulatory frameworks.

415.notes:
Machine Alignment, Transparency, and Security (MATS) is an independent research and educational seminar program founded in late 2021. The program connects talented researchers with top mentors in AI alignment, transparency, and security. MATS is led by Co-Executive Directors Ryan Kidd and Christian Smith, with offices in Berkeley, California and London, UK.

The program runs 12-week fully-funded research fellowships. Fellows receive a $15,000 stipend plus $12,000 in compute budget. MATS has trained over 527 researchers since its founding, with 80% of alumni working in AI alignment, transparency, and security. Approximately 10% of alumni have co-founded AI safety organizations including Apollo Research, Leap Labs, Timaeus, and others. 

MATS connects fellows with mentors from leading AI labs including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, UK AISI, and other organizations. The program consists of multiple phases, with fellows conducting research while attending talks, workshops, and networking events with the AI research community.

MATS has produced 180+ research publications. Fellows are eligible for up to 14 months of funding, with an initial 10-week program followed by an optional 6-12 month extension.

The organization is funded by Open Philanthropy, Survival and Flourishing Fund, Manifund, BERI, and other philanthropic sources. MATS originally stood for "ML Alignment & Theory Scholars" before rebranding to Machine Alignment, Transparency, and Security.
415.regulatory_stance_detail: MATS trains researchers in AI safety, alignment, interpretability, governance, and security with focus on reducing risks from unaligned AI. Program explicitly aims to address 'the world's most urgent and talent-constrained problem: reducing risks from unaligned artificial intelligence.' Research includes AI control, monitoring, evaluations, and governance policy work.
415.threat_models: Loss of control, Existential risk, National security

416.notes: Founded 2022 as Effective Ventures project. 8-week online fellowship for ages 14-20 tackling global challenges. Awards up to $30,000 in scholarships annually, with over $400,000 distributed since founding. Funded primarily by Open Philanthropy. Stanford HAI has funneled more than $40 million to support over 300 Stanford scholars across disciplines. In the U.S. AI policy ecosystem, HAI plays an influential role through its policy work: its faculty and researchers regularly advise Congress and federal agencies, with programs including the Congressional Boot Camp on AI that trains senior congressional staffers. The institute advocates for AI that augments rather than replaces humans, and provides evidence-based research to inform AI governance.

533.notes:
The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) is a government research organisation within the UK's Department for Science, Innovation and Technology. Originally established as the AI Safety Institute in November 2023, it was renamed to the AI Security Institute in February 2025. 

The institute's mission is to equip governments with a scientific understanding of the risks posed by advanced AI, particularly focusing on security risks such as AI-assisted development of chemical and biological weapons, cyberattacks, and AI-enabled crime.

Under Chair Ian Hogarth, a tech investor and entrepreneur, and Interim Director Adam Beaumont, formerly GCHQ's Chief AI Officer, the institute employs over 100 technical staff. These include alumni from organizations such as OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and the University of Oxford.

AISI has launched several major funding programs, including the Alignment Project which grew from an initial £15 million to over £27 million with support from partners including OpenAI, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, Anthropic, and others. The institute also runs the Systemic Safety Grants programme (£8.5 million announced) and the Challenge Fund (£5 million).

The institute has formal research partnerships with several leading AI companies. It has signed Memorandums of Understanding with Anthropic, Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Cohere for collaborative research and model access.

AISI played a central role in producing the International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI in 2024, coordinating input from 30 countries. The UK has been instrumental in the international AI Safety Summit process, hosting the first summit at Bletchley Park in November 2023 and co-hosting the Seoul Summit in May 2024 with South Korea.

540.notes: Public AI is a nonprofit initiative advocating for public-interest AI infrastructure as an alternative to commercial AI development. The organization positions AI as critical infrastructure analogous to public broadcasting or libraries, promoting government and civil-society funded AI projects and open models.

542.notes: Stanford RegLab (Regulation, Evaluation, and Governance Lab) partners with government agencies to design and evaluate programs, policies, and technologies that modernize government. The organization uses machine learning and data science to improve compliance, mass adjudication, policy making, and government services. RegLab has an extensive track record working with local and national government agencies including the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Santa Clara County Public Health Department, and others. Daniel E. Ho is the Faculty Director of RegLab and William Benjamin Scott and Luna M. Scott Professor of Law at Stanford University.

544.notes: 165-page essay series published June 2024 by Leopold Aschenbrenner, a former researcher on OpenAI's Superalignment team who was fired in April 2024. Argues AGI is "strikingly plausible" by 2027 by extrapolating GPT-2 → GPT-4 capability gains in compute, algorithmic efficiency, and "unhobbling," that a subsequent intelligence explosion could compress a decade of AI research into one year, and that the free world faces an existential race with the CCP over superintelligence. Became the defining national-security AI narrative in DC policy circles, heavily cited by hawks arguing for export controls, AI-lab security mandates, and a "Manhattan Project" posture on AI. Aschenbrenner has since launched an AGI-focused investment firm.
544.author: Leopold Aschenbrenner
544.key_argument: AGI is imminent; the US must win the race against China or face catastrophic consequences

545.notes: Seventh annual AI Index Report, published April 2024 by Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered AI (HAI). The 2024 edition documented industry dominance of frontier ML research (51 notable models from industry in 2023 vs. 15 from academia), surging training costs (GPT-4 ≈ $78M, Gemini Ultra ≈ $191M), an ~8× jump in generative-AI private investment to $25.2B, a proliferation of national AI regulations, and introduced a new chapter on AI in science and medicine. Widely treated as the canonical reference on the state of the AI ecosystem; cited routinely in congressional testimony, executive-branch AI policy documents, and industry research.
545.author: Stanford HAI
545.key_argument: Comprehensive annual benchmarking of AI progress, investment, policy, and public opinion

546.notes: Essay by Marc Andreessen (June 2023) arguing that AI will be a profoundly positive force for humanity, countering doomer narratives with a case for accelerating AI development.
546.author: Marc Andreessen
546.key_argument: AI risk is overstated by incumbents seeking regulatory moats; AI will generate enormous prosperity

548.notes: White paper published May 25, 2023 by Microsoft under a foreword from Vice Chair and President Brad Smith. Part 1 lays out a five-point blueprint for AI public policy: build on government AI safety frameworks (e.g. NIST AI RMF), require "safety brakes" on AI systems controlling critical infrastructure, adopt a layered regulatory model distinguishing the applications / model / infrastructure layers of the tech stack, pursue transparency and a broader public AI governance architecture, and leverage AI to address societal challenges. Part 2 describes Microsoft's internal responsible-AI program. One of the first major corporate AI policy statements from a frontier-model developer; cited in congressional AI Insight Forums and in international AI governance coordination discussions.
548.author: Microsoft (Brad Smith)
548.key_argument: Proposes tiered governance framework based on AI capability levels

549.notes: One-sentence open letter published May 30, 2023 by the Center for AI Safety (CAIS): “Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.” Signed by 350+ AI researchers and public figures, including Sam Altman, Demis Hassabis, Dario Amodei, Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Stuart Russell, and Bill Gates. A watershed moment that moved existential AI risk from a fringe concern into mainstream policy discourse.
549.author: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
549.key_argument: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war

550.notes: Voluntary framework published January 2023 by NIST (under Dept. of Commerce) providing guidance for organizations to manage risks from AI systems across the lifecycle. Built around four core functions — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage — and accompanied by the AI RMF Playbook and Generative AI Profile (July 2024). Widely adopted as the de facto U.S. industry reference; explicitly invoked in Biden's EO 14110 and in subsequent federal agency AI policies. Under the Trump administration's July 2025 AI Action Plan, NIST was directed to revise the RMF (removing references to DEI, misinformation, and climate change).
550.author: NIST
550.key_argument: Voluntary framework for managing AI risks throughout the AI lifecycle

551.notes: "On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big? 🦜" — peer-reviewed paper presented at ACM FAccT 2021 by Emily M. Bender (U. Washington), Timnit Gebru, Angelina McMillan-Major, and Margaret Mitchell. Argues that ever-larger language models carry four underappreciated costs: environmental impact from compute, unaccountable bias baked into uncurated web-scale training data, research opportunity cost, and downstream harms from fluent but meaning-blind outputs (the "stochastic parrot" metaphor — pattern matching without understanding). Foundational text of the algorithmic-harms / AI ethics wing of the field; internal dispute over the paper precipitated Gebru's forced exit from Google in December 2020 and Mitchell's firing in February 2021, becoming a watershed moment in the politics of industry AI research.
551.author: Emily Bender, Timnit Gebru, et al.
551.key_argument: Large language models pose environmental, bias, and misinformation risks that are inadequately addressed

552.notes: 2020 book by journalist and researcher Brian Christian (W.W. Norton, October 2020) structured in three parts: Prophecy (fairness, bias, and transparency failures in deployed ML systems — COMPAS, facial recognition, word embeddings), Agency (reinforcement learning, reward specification, and the difficulty of encoding objectives), and Normativity (imitation learning, inverse reward design, and long-horizon alignment of advanced AI). Widely cited as the most accessible bridge between mainstream ML-ethics literature and the AI-safety / long-term alignment community; frequently assigned as an introductory text in AI governance and technology-policy courses.
552.author: Brian Christian
552.key_argument: Comprehensive overview of the AI alignment challenge, from fairness to existential risk

633.notes: On July 23, 2025, the White House released 'America's AI Action Plan,' a 25-page document focused on bolstering U.S. AI dominance through deregulation, ideologically neutral AI systems, infrastructure investment, and international competition. Released alongside three executive orders covering AI development, federal procurement, and infrastructure. The Action Plan was issued pursuant to Executive Order 14179 ('Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence,' signed January 23, 2025), which mandated the creation of a comprehensive AI action plan within 180 days. EO 14179 also revoked Biden's Executive Order 14110 on AI safety.

643.notes: 2019 book by UC Berkeley computer scientist Stuart Russell arguing that the standard model of AI — machines pursuing fixed objectives — is fundamentally unsafe as capability scales, and proposing a provably-beneficial alternative in which AI systems remain uncertain about human preferences and defer to human feedback. Widely cited in AI governance discussions of alignment, oversight, and the case for safety-focused regulation. A foundational popular-audience text alongside Bostrom's Superintelligence.
643.author: Stuart Russell
643.key_argument: Current AI paradigm of fixed objectives is fundamentally dangerous; need provably beneficial AI

653.notes:
Published 3 February 2026 (DSIT 2026/001) ahead of the India AI Impact Summit. 200 pages, 1,451 references. Second annual edition in an ongoing series.

Secretariat: UK AI Security Institute (within DSIT), which has pledged to host until a long-term international home is established. The institute rebranded from "AI Safety Institute" between the 2025 and 2026 editions.

Chair: Yoshua Bengio. Lead writers: Stephen Clare and Carina Prunkl. Senior advisers span Daron Acemoglu, Geoffrey Hinton, Stuart Russell, Andrew Yao, and Yi Zeng.

Series history: May 2024 Interim Report (ahead of Seoul Summit); 29 January 2025 first full annual (DSIT 2025/001, ahead of France AI Action Summit); 15 October 2025 First Key Update on Capabilities and Risk Implications (arXiv:2510.13653); 25 November 2025 Second Key Update on Technical Safeguards and Risk Management (arXiv:2511.19863); 3 February 2026 second full annual.

Scope: risk taxonomy covers misuse (bio/chem uplift, cyberattacks, influence operations), malfunctions (loss of control, bias, reliability), and systemic risks (labor markets, market concentration, environmental, privacy). Deliberately makes no policy recommendations.
653.author: Yoshua Bengio, Stephen Clare, Carina Prunkl
653.key_argument: The first comprehensive international scientific synthesis of what general-purpose AI systems can do, what risks they pose, and how those risks can be managed. Mandated by the 2023 Bletchley AI Safety Summit and chaired by Yoshua Bengio, it is written by 100+ independent experts from 30+ countries plus the EU, OECD, and UN. Explicitly an evidence base for global decision-makers, not policy recommendations.

654.author: Zvi Mowshowitz
654.key_argument: Comprehensive weekly analysis of AI developments with focus on safety and existential risk.

655.author: Dario Amodei

In March 2026, AWS CEO Andy Jassy stated during an internal all-hands meeting that AI could help AWS reach $600 billion in annual sales by 2036, double his previous estimate of $300 billion. While previously supporting risk-based approaches for high-risk use cases, their 2025 position emphasizes that 'regulation tends to retard progress.'

730.regulatory_stance_detail: Emphasizes data sovereignty and privacy-first AI deployment with edge-native solutions that avoid cloud dependencies and vendor lock-in, suggesting preference for minimal regulatory interference while maintaining user control.

960.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for data coalitions and collective bargaining structures to redistribute AI power, while supporting open source models and targeted regulation through trusted data intermediaries rather than broad AI restrictions.

961.notes: Taiwan''s Ministry of Digital Affairs (MoDA), established August 2022, is the cabinet-level ministry responsible for digital development, cybersecurity, and AI policy in Taiwan. Audrey Tang served as its first minister (2022–2024) and made it a widely cited example of participatory digital governance, open-source civic tech, and democratic AI policymaking.
961.regulatory_stance_detail: Takes a principle-based approach to AI regulation through the AI Fundamental Act, establishing seven governance principles while promoting innovation through subsidies and regulatory sandboxes. Balances development with security through risk classification frameworks.

962.notes: Co-authored influential 2026 Hamilton Project report 'Building Pro-Worker Artificial Intelligence' defining framework for AI that augments rather than replaces human expertise. Served on National Academy committee for 2024 report 'Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Work.' Recognized as 'academic voice of the American worker' by Economist magazine and received 2019 Carnegie Fellowship for work on globalization and technology impacts on labor markets.
962.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for proactive government intervention to steer AI development toward 'pro-worker' applications through targeted sectoral policies, especially in healthcare and education, tax code reforms to reduce bias toward automation, and stronger safety nets like wage insurance for displaced workers.
962.threat_models: Labor displacement, Economic inequality, Power concentration

963.notes: Leading labor economist studying AI's impact on employment through the 'Race Between Education and Technology' framework. His research shows AI may substitute for entry-level workers while complementing experienced workers with tacit knowledge. Named 2025 Citation Laureate alongside David Autor for influential work on wages, inequality, and technological change. Co-authored influential book 'The Race between Education and Technology' (2008) with Claudia Goldin documenting how educational expansion affects inequality.
963.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for targeted policies to address AI-driven labor displacement, drawing parallels to past trade adjustment programs. Supports strengthening worker bargaining power and robust safety nets, while emphasizing the need for high-quality sectoral training programs to help displaced workers transition to new roles.

964.notes: Warns of AI bubble that could burst while simultaneously displacing workers, creating worst-case scenario without proper retraining infrastructure. Distinguishes between 'AI' (replacement) and 'IA' (intelligence assisting), advocating for latter approach. Signed Global Call for AI Red Lines in 2026. Predicts AI will primarily impact routine white-collar jobs while augmenting rather than replacing roles in education, healthcare, and skilled trades.
964.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for government regulation to prevent AI from exacerbating inequality and undermining information quality, while supporting AI as a tool for augmenting human capabilities. Calls for compensation mechanisms for news industry affected by AI scraping and international red lines for dangerous AI applications.

965.notes: Co-authored influential books 'Prediction Machines' (2018) and 'Power and Prediction' (2022) framing AI as primarily a prediction technology with economic implications. Founded Creative Destruction Lab, one of the world's largest seed-stage programs for science-based companies with over 600 startups admitted in 2022. Member of the Order of Canada (2022) and recipient of University of Toronto's President's Impact Award (2023). Advocates for viewing AI through economic lens of falling prediction costs rather than focusing on AGI scenarios.
965.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for an FDA-like regulatory approval process for AI applications in already-regulated sectors (insurance, healthcare) to provide clarity and accelerate investment, while allowing market forces to govern areas not currently regulated by humans. Supports applying existing regulations to AI rather than creating new broad frameworks.

966.notes: Published multiple NBER working papers on AI regulation including 'Can Socially-Minded Governance Control the AGI Beast?' (2024) concluding that socially-minded entities cannot minimize harm from unrestricted AGI products. Provides expert witness testimony in antitrust cases and has equity/advisory relationships with startup firms. Argues that ASI is unlikely to kill humans because we find AI economically valuable and wouldn't threaten its existence.
966.regulatory_stance_detail: Argues that ex post regulatory instruments like liability regimes outperform ex ante restrictions in many scenarios. Advocates for acceleration of AI adoption to surface and react to potential harms more quickly through 'learning by doing' rather than delayed adoption until harms are fully understood.
966.threat_models: Economic inequality, Power concentration, Loss of control

Previously worked in British government including Prime Minister's Strategy Unit and Cabinet Office. His TED Talk on the future of work has over 1.5 million views.
967.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for thoughtful policy responses to AI's labor market impacts, including consideration of Universal Basic Income and Job Guarantee Schemes. Emphasizes need for governments to prepare for AI-driven economic transformation rather than restrictive regulation of AI development itself.

Warns that AI monopolists could create scenario where wages fall to zero while goods remain expensive. Has consulted for Microsoft on competition topics unrelated to AI and regularly advises governments on confidential antitrust cases.
968.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for vigorous antitrust enforcement and competition policy to prevent AI monopolization, particularly through immediate enforcement action before markets concentrate. Supports pro-competitive regulation like interoperability requirements and open-source model promotion, while opposing broad bans in favor of targeted interventions.
968.threat_models: Power concentration, Economic inequality, Labor displacement

969.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for managing the speed and process of AI adoption through policy interventions like shifting taxes from labor to consumption/capital, implementing digital dividends, and ensuring competitive markets, while avoiding stopping AI development entirely.
969.threat_models: Labor displacement, Economic inequality, Power concentration

Co-authored economic modeling work on AI's wage and output impacts with complementarity between physical and intelligence sectors.
970.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for targeted regulation addressing AI's labor market impacts through safety nets and competition policy, proposing a two-tier system with AI Adjustment Insurance and Digital Dividend rather than broad AI restrictions.

971.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for leveraging existing regulatory tools and authorities rather than rushing new regulations, emphasizing 'guardrails and triggers' approach that establishes foundational rules while preparing escalation mechanisms based on how AI technology and markets evolve.

972.threat_models: Power concentration, Loss of control, Economic inequality

973.threat_models: Power concentration, Economic inequality, Labor displacement

974.notes: Served as Obama's chief economist and played major role in economic policies 2013-2017. Advocates six principles for AI regulation including application-specific approaches and comparing AI performance to imperfect humans rather than perfection.
974.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for application-specific AI regulation through existing agencies rather than federal-level blanket rules, emphasizing competition policy and merger enforcement over broad restrictions. Supports pro-competitive regulation including codes of conduct for dominant platforms and data mobility requirements.

975.notes: Goldfarb testified before the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee in May 2019 on digital advertising and data privacy, arguing that privacy regulation often creates trade-offs with innovation and competition. He co-authored influential books 'Prediction Machines' (2018) and 'Power and Prediction' that frame AI economically as cheap prediction technology, widely cited in policy discussions.
975.regulatory_stance_detail: Goldfarb advocates for careful regulatory design that balances innovation with legitimate concerns, emphasizing that privacy regulations often reduce innovation and that regulatory consistency is crucial. 976.notes: Testified before U.S. Senate AI Insight Forum arguing against regulating AI technology itself while supporting application-specific regulations. Publicly opposed California's SB 1047 and the White House's Defense Production Act use for AI regulation. 977.notes: Co-authored 2020 MIT report concluding AI mass unemployment fears are unlikely to be realized, instead predicting new job creation. Emphasizes AI as tool for human augmentation rather than replacement, advocating for policy frameworks that smooth workforce transitions.

979.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for ex ante licensing and regulatory approval for high-risk AI systems, proposing that firms should bear the burden of proving their AI is non-discriminatory and safe before deployment. Co-authored proposals for licensing high-risk AI with presumption of unlawfulness until justified.
979.threat_models: Power concentration, Economic inequality, Democratic erosion

Testified July 2024 before Senate Commerce Committee on AI privacy threats, warning about the 'inference economy' where AI derives intimate information from available data.
980.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for proactive, comprehensive AI regulation addressing specific harms rather than broad innovation-focused approaches. Supports sector-specific regulation combined with federal coordination, emphasizing protection from algorithmic bias, privacy violations, and corporate power concentration over speculative existential risks.

Testified before Senate Judiciary Committee in September 2023 advocating for moving beyond 'AI half-measures.' Published extensively on privacy law including 'Privacy's Blueprint' (2018) and co-authored 'The Great Scrape' on AI data collection practices. Served on Massachusetts Special Commission on Facial Recognition.
981.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for substantive legal protections against AI 'half-measures,' calling for duties of loyalty, design rules, and outright prohibitions on dangerous AI systems like emotion recognition, biometric surveillance, and social scoring. Testified before Congress that procedural approaches requiring only transparency and consent are insufficient.

Emphasizes pro-social AI governance through power-sharing liberalism framework.
982.threat_models: Power concentration, Democratic erosion, Economic inequality

983.notes: Nathaniel Persily is the James B. McClatchy Professor of Law at Stanford Law School and Co-Director of the Stanford Law AI Initiative. Persily co-authored "Social Media and Democracy: The State of the Field and Prospects for Reform" with Joshua Tucker, published by Cambridge University Press in 2020. He was awarded a Guggenheim Fellowship in 2020 for his work examining technology's impact on democracy. His recent research on AI and democracy argues that panic over AI could harm democracy more than AI itself, advocating for transparency, accountability, and significant public investment to guide AI's democratic development. He is co-editor of "The Digitalist Papers: Artificial Intelligence and Democracy in America" (2024) with Erik Brynjolfsson, Alex Pentland, and Condoleezza Rice.
983.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for targeted AI regulation informed by lessons from social media regulation, emphasizing transparency, accountability, researcher access, and public investment while warning against both under-regulation and panic-driven overregulation that could harm democracy.

Liability for AI Output' (2023). Argues that Section 230 protections don't apply to AI-generated content since it's created by the companies themselves, not third parties. Has testified as expert witness and provided analysis on California's AI training data disclosure law (AB 2013), finding it likely constitutional under First Amendment commercial speech doctrine.

Argues that AI speech should be protected based on users' rights to listen and speak, even if AI companies lack direct speech rights. Generally skeptical of government regulation that would restrict AI expression.

985.notes: Co-authored influential Science paper 'Large AI models are cultural and social technologies' (March 2025) arguing against AGI narratives. 985.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for treating AI as a social technology requiring complex governance reforms rather than simple restrictions, emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary approaches that combine social science with computer science to address AI's integration into existing institutions like markets, bureaucracy, and democracy.
985.threat_models: Power concentration, Democratic erosion, Economic inequality

Author of 'Open Democracy' and advocates for 'politics without politicians' through sortition-based citizen rule.
986.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for democratic governance of AI through citizen assemblies and participatory processes rather than pure industry self-regulation or heavy-handed state control. 986.threat_models: Democratic erosion, Power concentration, Economic inequality

Emphasizes preparing society for AI's disruptive effects on institutional mechanisms rather than trying to contain the technology's spread through export controls.

Advocates for 'reserved sociability' in digital civic platforms and human-centric AI governance.

Published 'Our Next Reality' (Hachette Books) on AI-XR convergence and spent decade leading HTC's VR business in China.

The book argues that creating superintelligent AI using current techniques would likely result in human extinction. Soares is the President of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI), where he has been working on AI alignment for over a decade. MIRI was founded in 2000, predating major AI companies like OpenAI and DeepMind. Prior to joining MIRI in 2014, Soares worked as a software engineer at Google and Microsoft. He also worked as a research associate at the National Institute of Standards and Technology and as a contractor for the US Department of Defense. Soares argues that modern AI systems are "grown" rather than carefully crafted, making them fundamentally difficult to control.
999.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for an international treaty to ban the race to superintelligence, arguing that governments should agree to a worldwide freeze on advanced AI research capabilities. Supports allowing narrow AI applications like self-driving cars and medical tech while stopping the development of artificial general intelligence.

1000.notes:
Sundar Pichai has served as CEO of Google since August 2015 and CEO of Alphabet since December 2019. Born on June 10, 1972, in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, India, he grew up in Chennai and earned a bachelor's degree in metallurgical engineering from IIT Kharagpur in 1993, where he received an Institute Silver Medal. He holds a master's degree in materials science and engineering from Stanford University (1995) and an MBA from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania (2002), where he was named both a Siebel Scholar and a Palmer Scholar.

Pichai joined Google in 2004 and led the development of key products including the Chrome browser and Android operating system. In 2025, Google announced a $15 billion investment over five years (2026-2030) to establish an AI hub in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, marking the company's largest investment in India to date. The facility will include gigawatt-scale data center operations and an international subsea gateway.

In 2025, Pichai achieved billionaire status with a net worth exceeding $1.1 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. His 2022 total compensation was $226 million, which included $218 million in stock awards as part of a triennial grant. Under his leadership, Google launched its Gemini AI model in December 2023, with the Bard chatbot subsequently rebranded as Gemini in February 2024.
1000.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for comprehensive AI regulation while maintaining innovation. Testified before Congress supporting national AI legislation to avoid state-by-state patchwork that could weaken US competitiveness against China. Calls for 'well-regulated' AI deployment to prevent harmful effects, supports consequences for deepfakes, and established Google's AI principles in 2018 prohibiting weaponry applications. Urges Congress to pass unified national AI framework balancing safety with progress.

1001.notes: Led Microsoft's $13 billion investment in OpenAI partnership beginning with an initial $1 billion investment in 2019, followed by additional investments in 2021 and 2023. Microsoft and OpenAI established a joint Deployment Safety Board in 2021 for pre-release safety reviews of AI models. Under his leadership, Microsoft has nearly 350 employees working on responsible AI as of 2023, growing to over 400 by 2024. At the White House AI Safety convening in July 2023, Microsoft made voluntary commitments including annual transparency reporting and pre-deployment safety testing of AI systems.
1001.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for applying existing sector-specific regulations to AI (e.g., healthcare regulations for healthcare AI, financial regulations for financial AI) rather than creating new comprehensive AI legislation. Supports global coordination on AI standards and norms, comparing needed governance to IAEA for nuclear technology. Emphasizes risk-based deployment assessment, rigorous red teaming for large language models, and industry responsibility for safety while avoiding over-regulation.
1001.threat_models: Economic inequality, Misinformation, Loss of control

1002.notes: Former Google Design Ethicist who authored a 141-slide presentation titled 'A Call to Minimize Distraction & Respect Users' Attention' in February 2013. Featured in Netflix's 'The Social Dilemma' documentary in 2020. Named to Time 100 Next Leaders in 2021 and Rolling Stone's 25 People Shaping the World in 2017. Co-hosts 'Your Undivided Attention' podcast. Studied Computer Science at Stanford University.
1002.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for restrictive AI regulation including making recursive self-improvement illegal with jail time, mandatory safety testing before deployment, whistleblower protections, transparency requirements, and international coordination comparable to nuclear weapons treaties. Compares current AI development to 'racing to build a super intelligent digital god.' Has testified before Congress multiple times and advocates for narrow AI applications over general autonomous systems.
1002.threat_models: Existential risk, Loss of control, Misinformation

1003.notes: Co-founder of Center for Humane Technology (2018) and Earth Species Project (2017), focusing on AI-animal communication translation. Subject and architect of Emmy-winning Netflix documentary 'The Social Dilemma' (2020). Created infinite scroll technology while at Mozilla. Trained as mathematician and dark matter physicist at University of Chicago (BS) and Caltech (PhD program). Son of Macintosh co-creator Jef Raskin. Co-hosts 'Your Undivided Attention' podcast. Featured on Oprah's AI special (2024). Former head of UX at Mozilla Labs, founded multiple companies including Humanized (acquired by Mozilla), Songza, and Massive Health (acquired by Jawbone). Columbia operates the Center of Artificial Intelligence Technology in collaboration with Amazon, guided by the Engineering for Humanity vision. The university was founded as King's College in 1754 and renamed Columbia University in the City of New York in 1896.

1049.notes: The University of Washington is comprised of three campuses: the Seattle campus with sixteen schools and colleges, plus the Bothell and Tacoma campuses. The primary mission of the University of Washington is the preservation, advancement, and dissemination of knowledge. The UW has been recognized as the #1 most innovative public university in the world and receives more federal research dollars than any other U.S. public university. The University was founded on November 4, 1861, making it one of the oldest state-supported institutions of higher education on the Pacific coast.

1050.notes: MIT Sloan is the MIT Sloan School of Management, located in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States. The school employs 1,398 people and operates in 49 countries. Richard M. Locke is the John C Head III Dean at MIT Sloan, beginning his appointment as dean in July 2025. MIT Sloan offers various programs including MBA, Executive Education, and specialized programs like the MIT Sloan Fellows MBA Program.

1051.notes: The Center for Humane Technology is a nonprofit organization founded in 2018 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, dedicated to radically reimagining digital infrastructure and driving a comprehensive shift toward humane technology. The organization was co-founded by Tristan Harris and Aza Raskin, with Harris previously serving as a Design Ethicist at Google where he created the viral presentation 'A Call to Minimize Distraction & Respect Users' Attention'. CHT employs 22 people and focuses on transforming the incentives that drive technology, from social media to artificial intelligence, working to catalyze systems-level change in the tech ecosystem. The organization has launched a new area of work called 'AI and What Makes Us Human' to address what new norms, legal protections, and fundamental rights are needed to preserve what makes life meaningful in the age of AI.

1052.notes: The Distributed Artificial Intelligence Research Institute (DAIR) is a research institute founded by Timnit Gebru in December 2021. The institute describes itself as "an independent, community-rooted institute set to counter Big Tech's pervasive influence on the research, development and deployment of AI." In February 2022, two members of Google's Ethical AI research group, researcher Alex Hanna and software engineer Dylan Baker, left Google to join DAIR. DAIR is an interdisciplinary and globally distributed AI research institute rooted in the belief that AI is not inevitable, its harms are preventable, and when its production and deployment include diverse perspectives and deliberate processes it can be beneficial.

1053.notes: Mila is the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute, recognized worldwide for its major contributions to AI. The institute boasts the largest concentration of deep learning academic researchers globally and is described as the world's largest academic research center for deep learning. The institute is a community of more than 1,400 researchers specializing in machine learning and dedicated to scientific excellence and innovation. Mila is the result of a unique collaboration between Université de Montréal and McGill University, in close collaboration with Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal. The institute also hosts professors from Université Laval, Université de Sherbrooke, École de technologie supérieure, and Concordia University. Founded by Professor Yoshua Bengio in 1993, Mila acquired the status of non-profit organization in 2018.

1054.notes: Nonprofit developer of the Signal encrypted-messaging app. President Meredith Whittaker argues AI is fundamentally a surveillance technology that expands harmful data-collection business models. Signal has publicly warned that agentic AI poses an existential threat to secure messaging, and opposes mandatory message-scanning laws such as the EU Chat Control proposal.

1055.notes:
The Gates Foundation is an American private foundation founded by Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates. Based in Seattle, Washington, it was launched in 2000 through the merger of the William H. Gates Foundation and the Gates Learning Foundation. The foundation is reported to be the third-wealthiest charitable foundation in the world, holding $86 billion in assets as of July 31, 2025. 

The foundation's stated goals are to enhance healthcare and reduce extreme poverty across the world, and to expand educational opportunities and access to information technology in the United States. In January 2025, the foundation changed its name from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation to the Gates Foundation.

On May 8, 2025, Bill Gates announced that he will donate virtually all of his remaining wealth—approximately $200 billion—to the foundation over the next 20 years. He also announced that the foundation will close its doors on December 31, 2045. This represents a change from the foundation's original charter, which stated it would sunset 20 years after Gates' death.

The foundation's governing board approved a budget of $8.74 billion for 2025, which is the largest budget in its history. The foundation is on track to reach annual distributions of $9 billion in 2026.

1056.notes: Emerson Collective, LLC is an American company founded by Laurene Powell Jobs in 2011 in Palo Alto, California. The company invests in entrepreneurs and innovators working in education, energy and the environment, immigration, media and journalism. Emerson Collective has invested in at least nine AI startups since 2022, with involvement in AI funding rounds totaling over $1 billion. The organization operates as a limited liability company and focuses on venture capital investment and philanthropy.

1057.notes: AngelList is building the infrastructure that powers the startup economy and aims to accelerate innovation by providing startups and investors with the connected tools they need to launch and scale a startup or fund—and invest in both. AngelList reaches over $171B in assets on the platform, with over 72k investors, 13k active startups, and more than 25k funds and syndicates supported. AngelList is the parent company of AngelList Venture, AngelList Talent, and Product Hunt and has more than 20 unicorns in the portfolio. The company provides investors and innovators with the tools to grow, offering venture funds, SPVs, scout funds, and digital subscriptions.

1058.notes:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey, alongside co-founders Trae Stephens, Matt Grimm, Joe Chen, and Brian Schimpf. The company builds AI-powered autonomous weapons, surveillance systems, and battlefield software centered around its Lattice platform. 

In June 2025, Anduril raised $2.5 billion in a Series G funding round led by Founders Fund, achieving a valuation of $30.5 billion. As of March 2026, the company is reportedly raising a new funding round co-led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, targeting a valuation of approximately $60 billion.

On March 13, 2026, the U.S. Army awarded Anduril a 10-year enterprise contract with a ceiling of up to $20 billion, consolidating more than 120 separate procurement actions around Lattice. The first task order under this contract was an $87 million award from Joint Interagency Task Force 401 for counter-UAS command and control.

According to Sacra estimates, Anduril achieved $2.1 billion in revenue in 2025, representing 110% year-over-year growth, with projections of $4.3 billion for 2026. Palmer Luckey has publicly opposed corporate restrictions on military AI use, arguing that elected government—not corporate executives—should set AI weapons policy.

1059.notes: The New York Times is a media organization dedicated to seeking the truth and helping people understand the world through independent journalism. The company has over 11.4 million subscribers and employs approximately 2,000 journalists in its newsroom. The New York Times has created an A.I. Initiatives team led by Editorial Director Zach Seward to leverage artificial intelligence for journalism while maintaining human oversight. The organization filed a lawsuit against Perplexity AI for unauthorized use of Times content.

1060.notes: Independent tech newsletter founded in 2020 by Casey Newton, focusing on the intersection of technology and democracy. Covers major AI labs and platforms with a critical, product-focused lens. Subscriber-funded via Ghost; Newton declined Substack advances and moved the publication off Substack in 2024 over content moderation concerns.

1061.notes: Common Sense Media is an American nonprofit organization founded by Jim Steyer in 2003 that reviews and provides ratings for media and technology with the goal of providing information on their suitability for children. The organization is headquartered in San Francisco, California and is dedicated to improving the lives of kids and families by providing trustworthy information, education, and independent voice they need to thrive. Common Sense Media rates movies, TV shows, books, and more so parents can feel good about the entertainment choices they make for their kids, and offers the largest, most trusted library of independent age-based ratings and reviews. The organization also advocates publicly for child-friendly policies and laws regarding media and education, and funds research on the role of media in the lives of children.

1062.notes: Research initiative co-founded by Eli Pariser and Talia Stroud, originally a project of the National Conference on Citizenship and the Center for Media Engagement at UT Austin. Developed a framework of 14 design principles ("signals") for evaluating and building healthier digital public spaces, based on a 20-country YouGov survey of 20,000+ people funded by the Omidyar Network. Rebranded as New_Public in 2021 and continues work on digital public infrastructure. Advocates for treating digital spaces like physical public infrastructure (libraries, parks, town squares) with civic design principles. Jennifer Pahlka is affiliated (edge: employer).

1063.notes: The Amazon Labor Union (ALU) was founded by warehouse workers at the JFK8 Fulfillment Center in Staten Island, New York, and is now known as Amazon Labor Union–IBT Local 1. The NLRB recently ordered Amazon.com Services to bargain with Amazon Labor Union at a fulfillment center located in Staten Island, N.Y. (JFK8 Facility). Chris Smalls is identified as the Amazon Labor Union founder who wrote a book called 'When the Revolution Comes'. The union operates as a worker-led union committed to transforming conditions at Amazon and describes itself as a fighting union built by and for Amazon workers.

1064.notes: The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) is a private, nonprofit organization that facilitates cutting-edge research on and analysis of major economic issues, founded in New York City in 1920 and today headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The NBER is a network of more than 1,800 academic economists, with 43 current or former NBER affiliates having been awarded the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, and 13 have chaired the President's Council of Economic Advisers. The organization recently conducted a study surveying nearly 6,000 top executives across the US, UK, Germany and Australia about AI's impact on employment and productivity. The current president and chief executive officer is MIT professor of economics James Poterba.

1065.notes: Google Brain was a deep learning artificial intelligence research team that served as the sole AI branch of Google before being incorporated under the newer umbrella of Google AI, a research division at Google dedicated to artificial intelligence. Formed in 2011, it combined open-ended machine learning research with information systems and large-scale computing resources. It was merged into former Google sister company DeepMind to form Google DeepMind in April 2023. Google Brain was initially established by Google Fellow Jeff Dean and visiting Stanford professor Andrew Ng.

1066.notes: Google Research is the research division of Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc. According to its official website, Google Research publishes findings, releases open-source software, and applies research results within Google products and services as well as within the wider scientific community. Google Research maintains a portfolio of research projects driven by fundamental research, new product innovation, product contribution and infrastructure goals. The organization is led by Yossi Matias, Vice President & Head of Google Research.

1067.notes: The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a nonpartisan, independent national membership organization, think tank, educator, and publisher founded in 1921. CFR publishes Foreign Affairs magazine and generates policy-relevant ideas and analysis on the most consequential issues facing the United States and the world. The organization has 1,277 employees and an annual revenue of $77.3 million. CFR's mission is to inform U.S. engagement with the world and convenes experts and policymakers to promote informed public discussion.

1068.notes: The World Economic Forum is an independent, not-for-profit organization, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, with offices in New York and San Francisco, United States, Beijing, China, and Tokyo, Japan. Founded in 1971 as a not-for-profit foundation, the World Economic Forum set out with a transformative point of view: that business should not only to create economic value but also to serve society and the planet. The Forum is the International Organization for Public-Private Cooperation that engages the foremost political, business and other leaders of society to shape global, regional and industry agendas. The Forum has served as an impartial, globally respected platform for cooperation for more than five decades.

1069.notes: Microsoft Research is a multidisciplinary global organization working to create scientific knowledge and deliver innovation that leads to positive human impact at scale. Microsoft Research has shaped the technology people use every day for nearly 35 years through a commitment to hiring the world's top minds and giving them autonomy, resources, and support to conduct research. Microsoft Research has research labs across the globe and mission-focused efforts in areas like scientific discovery and human health, conducting fundamental science and technology research that benefits humanity. The organization was founded in 1991, with the Microsoft Research Plan memo from September 1991 serving as the catalyst for the development of the organization.

1070.notes: Facebook AI Research (FAIR) Paris was created in 2015 to advance the field of artificial intelligence through open research for the benefit of all. FAIR has grown into an international research organization with labs in Menlo Park, New York, Paris, Montreal, Tel Aviv, Seattle, Pittsburgh, and London. For more than a decade, Meta's Fundamental AI Research (FAIR) team has focused on advancing the state of the art in AI through open research. FAIR has applied an open model to all aspects of their work, collaborating broadly with the community by publishing cutting-edge research early and often, and open-sourcing research code, data sets, and tools like PyTorch, fastText, FAISS, and Detectron.

1071.notes: Tesla announced a joint project with xAI called Digital Optimus, also nicknamed 'Macrohard,' designed to automate complex office workflows by observing and replicating human interactions with computers. As part of this collaboration, Tesla entered into an agreement on January 16, 2026, to invest $2 billion in xAI. Tesla's financial performance declined significantly in 2025, with profits falling 46 percent and revenue dropping for the first time in the company's history. The company's automotive revenues fell by 11 percent to $17.7 billion in Q4 2025, while its energy storage business grew 25 percent.

1072.notes: Stripe was founded in 2010 by two Irish brothers, Patrick Collison (CEO) and John Collison (President), who came to the US in 2006 at ages 18 and 16 respectively. In 2025, businesses running on Stripe generated $1.9 trillion in total volume, up 34% from 2024, and equivalent to roughly 1.6% of global GDP. Stripe now powers more than 5 million businesses directly or via platforms, including 90% of the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 80% of the Nasdaq 100. The company has developed AI-focused products including the Stripe integration benchmark for evaluating AI agents' ability to build complete Stripe integrations, and the Agentic Commerce Suite for enabling businesses to sell on AI agents.

1073.notes: Palantir Technologies is a data analytics and AI company that builds software platforms for data integration and analysis, serving government and commercial clients. The company was founded in 2003 by Peter Thiel, Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale, Nathan Gettings, and Alex Karp, with Karp becoming CEO in 2005. Palantir's Maven AI system has been adopted by the Pentagon as a core military system for weapons targeting and battlefield data analysis. The company reported Q4 2025 revenue of $1.407 billion, up 70% year-over-year, with a market capitalization of $423.66 billion as of December 31, 2025.

1074.notes: DeepLearning.AI was founded in 2017 by Andrew Ng, a global leader in AI. The company is an education technology company that empowers the global workforce to build an AI-powered future through world-class education, hands-on training, and a collaborative community. DeepLearning.AI is making a world-class AI education accessible to people around the globe. The company is headquartered in Mountain View, California and employs 237 people.

1075.notes: Coursera was founded by Stanford University professors Andrew Ng and Daphne Koller in 2012. The company has grown to serve 197 million registered learners as of December 31, 2025. Coursera partners with over 375 leading university and industry partners to offer courses, specializations, professional certificates, and degrees. The company went public on the New York Stock Exchange in March 2021.

1076.notes: BlackRock is a global asset manager and technology provider with over $14 trillion in assets under management as of Q4 2025. The company has formed an AI Infrastructure Partnership with Microsoft, raising $12.5 billion toward a $30 billion goal. BlackRock has built an AI research platform dubbed 'Asimov' for use in its fundamental equity business. The company's CEO Larry Fink has framed AI as 'the most significant technology since, at least, the computer' in his 2026 annual letter to investors.

1077.notes: The University of Toronto is described as a world-leader in Artificial Intelligence (AI) research, including machine and deep learning, natural language processing, and computer vision. The university has established the Hinton Chair in Artificial Intelligence with $10 million in funding from Google, with U of T matching Google's support with an additional $10 million in funding. U of T ranked 21st globally in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2025 and is the top-ranked university in Canada. The university was founded in 1827 and has three campuses: St. George, Mississauga, and Scarborough.

1078.notes: Carnegie Mellon University was founded in 1900 by philanthropist Andrew Carnegie who donated $1 million to establish a school where students from all backgrounds could gain skills to uplift their careers and communities. The university was originally called Carnegie Technical Schools (1900-1912), then Carnegie Institute of Technology (1912-1967), and became Carnegie Mellon University in 1967 when Carnegie Tech merged with the Mellon Institute. Carnegie Mellon is described as the birthplace of AI over half a century ago and maintains the world's #1 ranked AI program.

1079.notes: Georgetown University is a Catholic and Jesuit, student-centered research university established in 1789. The university offers an online Master of Professional Studies in Artificial Intelligence Management through Georgetown SCS, which is a 30-credit program with tuition of $52,560. Georgetown has adopted Google Gemini for students, faculty and staff as part of its AI initiatives. The university has more than 22,000 undergraduate and graduate students who take classes at five locations: Main Campus, Medical Center, Law Center, School of Continuing Studies, and the university's Georgetown Qatar campus.

1080.notes: Yale University was founded in 1701 and is committed to improving the world today and for future generations through outstanding research and scholarship, education, preservation, and practice. Yale announced over $150 million in funding over five years to support faculty, students, and staff as they engage with artificial intelligence. The university is located in New Haven, Connecticut and has approximately 15,564 total students including 6,814 undergraduates and 8,750 graduate students. Yale's mission includes educating aspiring leaders worldwide who serve all sectors of society through the free exchange of ideas in an ethical, interdependent, and diverse community.

1081.notes: The United Nations is an international organization founded in 1945, currently made up of 193 Member States, with work guided by the purposes and principles contained in its founding Charter. The UN has established a High-Level Advisory Body on AI to analyze the current situation and recommend governance approaches for artificial intelligence. The General Assembly approved a $3.72 billion budget for the United Nations for 2025. The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco and came into force on 24 October, which is now recognized as UN Day.

1082.notes: The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states that are located primarily in Europe. The EU was established, along with its citizenship, when the Maastricht Treaty came into force in 1993, and was incorporated as an international legal juridical person upon entry into force of the Treaty of Lisbon in 2009. In 2012, the EU was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The European Union has enacted the Artificial Intelligence Act, which is a European Union regulation concerning artificial intelligence that entered into force on 1 August 2024.

1083.notes: DARPA is a research and development agency of the United States Department of Defense responsible for the development of emerging technologies for use by the military. The agency was created on February 7, 1958, by President Dwight D. Eisenhower in response to the Soviet's launch of Sputnik 1 in 1957. DARPA comprises about 220 government employees in six technical offices, including nearly 100 program managers. The agency's annual budget is $4.122 billion (FY2024).

1084.notes: The University of Michigan is a public research university in Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States, founded in 1817 and is the oldest institution of higher education in the state. The university reported record total enrollment of 52,855 students for fall 2024, with undergraduate enrollment of 34,454 students. U-M has annual research volume that exceeds $1.86 billion and employs 20,482 people. The university received a record number of applications for fall 2025 with more than 115,000 prospective first-year and transfer students.

1085.notes: UCLA has an AI Innovation Initiative that is a campus-wide effort to build AI fluency, foster innovation, and drive responsible AI adoption. The initiative includes strategic partnerships with leaders like OpenAI and Google to empower faculty, staff, and students. UCLA's primary purpose as a public research university is the creation, dissemination, preservation and application of knowledge for the betterment of our global society. The university operates on a quarter system with Fall, Winter, Spring quarters and Summer sessions.

1086.notes: Johns Hopkins University offers multiple artificial intelligence programs including an online Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence developed with expertise from the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Lab. The university also has a Johns Hopkins Data Science and AI Institute that focuses on research and education in data science, machine learning, and artificial intelligence across diverse fields. The university's mission is to educate students and cultivate their capacity for lifelong learning, to foster independent and original research, and to bring the benefits of discovery to the world. Johns Hopkins University was founded in 1876 with the inauguration of its first president, Daniel Coit Gilman.

1087.notes: The University of Louisville offers a Graduate Certificate in Artificial Intelligence in Medicine and a Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence in Medicine. The university was established in 1798. As a state-supported research university, it is located in Louisville, Kentucky's largest metropolitan area. As of Fall 2024, the university has a total student enrollment of 24,073. The university has three campuses, including the 274-acre Belknap Campus, the Health Sciences Center, and Shelby Campus.

1088.notes: American University is a private federally chartered research university in Washington, D.C., chartered by Congress in 1893. The university consists of eight schools and colleges, including the Kogod School of Business, School of International Service, College of Arts and Sciences, School of Communication, School of Professional and Extended Studies, School of Public Affairs, Linda A. and H. Kent Baker School of Education, and Washington College of Law. American University has 13,019 students as of fall 2023 and offers over 160 academic programs. The Kogod School of Business has launched the Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence (IAAI) and has been recognized for having 'the most consequential AI transformation in business education' according to Poets&Quants.

1089.notes: SUNY Albany is also known as University at Albany, UAlbany, or SUNY Albany and is a public research university in Albany, New York, United States. The university was founded in 1844 and is one of four "university centers" of the State University of New York (SUNY) system. In 2024, the university enrolled 17,567 students in nine schools and colleges, which offer over 50 undergraduate majors and over 150 graduate programs. The university is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research spending and doctorate production".

1090.notes: USC is a private university founded in 1880 that is home to more than 48,000 students and over 4,400 full-time faculty. USC launched the Frontiers of Computing initiative in 2023, a $1B-plus initiative for advanced computation, quantum computing, AI and ethics as the largest, most comprehensive academic initiative in USC's history. USC has multiple AI research centers and initiatives, including the USC Center for AI in Society founded in 2016, which is a collaboration between USC's Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work and Viterbi School of Engineering. The university provides every student, faculty member, staff member and researcher with secure, enterprise-grade AI tools.

1091.notes: The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania was founded in 1881 as the world's first collegiate business school. It has more than 235 renowned professors and 5,000 undergraduate, MBA, executive MBA, and doctoral students. In April 2025, Wharton announced a new undergraduate concentration and MBA major in Artificial Intelligence for Business. The school is led by Dean Erika James.

1092.notes: Tulane University is a private research university in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States that was founded as the Medical College of Louisiana in 1834 by a cohort of medical doctors. The institution became private under the endowments of Paul Tulane and Josephine Louise Newcomb in 1884 and 1887. Tulane has been a member of the Association of American Universities since 1958 and is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity". The university has established multiple AI-related initiatives including the Connolly Alexander Institute for Data Science, the Jurist Center for Artificial Intelligence, and the Center for Community-Engaged Artificial Intelligence.

1093.notes: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) is committed to safety and innovation and sees artificial intelligence (AI) as a promising capability to help achieve these aims. The Department has established an AI Compliance Plan in response to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-25-21, Accelerating Federal Use of AI through Innovation, Governance, and Public Trust. The Department was authorized in October 1966 and launched on 1 April 1967, with a mission to ensure that federal funds were effectively used to support the national transportation program. The mission of the USDOT is to ensure our nation has the safest, most efficient and modern transportation system in the world; that improves the quality of life for all American people and communities, from rural to urban, and increases the productivity and competitiveness of American workers and businesses.

1094.notes: Peter Norvig is a Distinguished Education Fellow at Stanford's Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence Institute and a researcher at Google Inc. He co-authored "Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach" with Stuart Russell, which is the leading textbook in the field used in more than 1,500 universities in 135 countries. He was born on December 14, 1956, and previously served as head of NASA Ames's Computational Sciences Division where he was NASA's senior computer scientist. He co-taught an online Artificial Intelligence class that signed up 160,000 students, helping to kick off massive open online classes.

1096.notes: The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF or UC San Francisco) is a public land-grant research university in San Francisco, California, United States that is part of the University of California system and is dedicated entirely to health science and life science. UCSF was founded as Toland Medical College in 1864, became affiliated with the University of California as its medical department in 1873, gained full administrative independence as a campus of the UC system in 1964, and gained its current name in 1970. UCSF's mission is to advance health worldwide through preeminent biomedical research, graduate-level education in the life sciences and health professions, and excellence in patient care. In 2023, UCSF received the 2nd highest research funding from the National Institutes of Health.

1097.notes: Bayesian Logic Inc. is co-founded by Nimar Arora, who serves as Chief Executive Officer, Secretary, Chief Financial Officer, and Director. Stuart Russell serves as a Director and is described as founder and Vice-President of the company. The company was officially filed as a General Corporation in California on October 24, 2011, and maintains active status. Bayesian Logic Inc. developed NET-VISA, a Bayesian seismic monitoring system for detecting nuclear explosions, which has been deployed by the CTBT organization of the U.N. and achieves around 60% reduction in missed events compared to currently deployed systems.

1098.notes: Michael Genesereth (born 1948) is an American logician and computer scientist, who is most known for his work on computational logic and applications of that work in enterprise management, computational law, and general game playing. Genesereth is professor in the Computer Science Department at Stanford University and a professor by courtesy in the Stanford Law School. His 1987 textbook on Logical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence remains one of the key references on symbolic artificial intelligence. He is the author of the influential Game Description Language(GDL) and Knowledge Interchange Format(KIF), the latter of which led to the ISO Common Logic standard.

1099.notes: Tom Cotton is a U.S. Senator representing Arkansas who introduced the DATA Act of 2026, which would allow AI data center companies to bypass federal electricity regulations by building independent energy infrastructure. Cotton stated that "American dominance in artificial intelligence and other crucial emerging industries should not come at the expense of Arkansans paying higher energy costs". On November 13, 2024, Senate Republicans selected Cotton as the next conference chair, making him the third-highest ranked Republican in the Senate. Cotton previously co-introduced a resolution with Senator Chris Coons to affirm America's artificial intelligence dominance.

1100.notes: Andy Kim is a U.S. Senator from New Jersey who serves as a Democrat on multiple committees including Commerce, Science, and Transportation. He has been actively involved in AI-related legislation, co-introducing the Artificial Intelligence Ready Data Act with Senator Ted Budd to open government data sets for training American AI models. Kim also co-introduced the AI Talent Act with Senator Jon Husted to create an AI and tech talent team within the U.S. Office of Personnel Management. He was born on July 12, 1982, in Boston, Massachusetts, to South Korean immigrant parents and is the first Korean American elected to the U.S. Senate.

1101.notes: Jim Risch is a U.S. Senator from Idaho who has served since 2009 and is a member of the Republican Party. He serves on five key committees: Energy and Natural Resources, Foreign Relations, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, Intelligence, and Ethics, and serves as Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. He previously served as Idaho's 31st Governor in 2006 and as Lieutenant Governor, and achieved major tax reform as Governor, cutting property taxes by 20%. He is consistently recognized as one of the most conservative members of the U.S. Senate.

1102.notes: Ben Horowitz is a cofounder and general partner at the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz. He previously co-founded and served as president and chief executive officer of the enterprise software company Opsware, which Hewlett-Packard acquired in 2007. Andreessen Horowitz recently raised more than $15 billion across five new funds, with Horowitz stating that at this moment of profound technological opportunity, it is fundamentally important for humanity that America wins. He has authored books including The Hard Thing About Hard Things: Building a Business When There Are No Easy Answers.

1103.notes: Donald Trump served as the 45th President of the United States from 2017 to 2021 and was inaugurated as the 47th president on January 20, 2025. On March 20, 2026, the Trump Administration released a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence that addresses six key objectives including protecting children, safeguarding American communities, and ensuring American AI dominance. In December 2025, President Trump signed an Executive Order to protect American AI innovation from inconsistent state laws and directed the Attorney General to establish an AI Litigation Task Force. Trump has appointed David Sacks as White House AI and Crypto Czar who has described the administration's AI policy focus areas as the '5 Cs': child safety, communities, creators, censorship, and competitiveness.

1104.notes: Coinbase is joining the x402 Foundation alongside tech titans like Amazon, Google, and Stripe. Coinbase has launched crypto wallet infrastructure that allows AI agents to spend, earn and trade crypto. The company's mission is to increase economic freedom for more than 1 billion people by providing a trusted platform for crypto assets. Coinbase delivered strong Q4 and full year 2024 results, with full year revenue of $6.6 billion, net income of $2.6 billion, and Adjusted EBITDA of $3.3 billion.

1105.notes: Sen. John Kennedy (R-LA) questioned David Evan Harris about AI regulation during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on September 17, 2024. Kennedy co-introduced the AI Labeling Act (S. 2691) with Sen. Brian Schatz (D-HI) on October 24, 2023, which would notify consumers when they interact with AI-generated content and require developers to disclose such content. Kennedy has introduced legislation to withhold senators' pay during government shutdowns, with the U.S. Senate Rules Committee unanimously advancing this proposal in December 2025. Kennedy reacted positively to President Trump's joint address to Congress in March 2025, stating "President Trump has given us a blueprint".

1106.notes: Cory Gardner is President & CEO of NCTA – The Internet & Television Association, beginning his tenure on September 22, 2025. He previously served as a U.S. Senator from Colorado from 2015 to 2021 and as a U.S. Representative for Colorado's 4th Congressional District from 2011 to 2015. Gardner served as chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee from 2017 to 2019. He was consistently ranked among the most bipartisan senators, including being ranked the 5th most bipartisan senator of the 115th Congress in March 2019.

1107.notes: The Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee is a standing committee of the United States Senate composed of 28 Senators and led by Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) and Ranking Member Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.). The committee has broad jurisdiction over all matters concerning interstate commerce, science and technology policy, and transportation, and is one of the largest of the Senate's standing committees. The committee has six subcommittees which together oversee issues ranging from communications, highways, aviation, rail, shipping, transportation security, merchant marine, the Coast Guard, oceans, fisheries, weather, disasters, science, space, interstate commerce, tourism, consumer issues, economic development, technology, competitiveness, product safety, and insurance. The committee passed the bipartisan Future of AI Innovation Act to maintain United States leadership in the global race to develop artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies.

1108.notes: The Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP) is a bipartisan, non-profit initiative with a mission to make recommendations to strengthen America's long-term competitiveness as artificial intelligence (AI) and other emerging technologies reshape national security, economy, and society. SCSP carries forward the vital mission of the National Security Commission on Artificial Intelligence (NSCAI), which was established in 2018. The organization was founded in 2021 and has 98 employees, located in Crystal City, United States. SCSP has launched multiple commissions and task forces, including collaborations with NVIDIA on AI and the future of work, and commissions on fusion energy and robotics for advanced manufacturing.

1109.notes: The Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Research (BAIR) Lab brings together UC Berkeley researchers across the areas of computer vision, machine learning, natural language processing, planning, and robotics. BAIR includes over two dozen faculty and more than a hundred graduate students pursuing research on fundamental advances in the above areas as well as cross-cutting themes including multi-modal deep learning, human-compatible AI, and connecting AI with other scientific disciplines and the humanities. The lab was established in 1990 as part of the University of California, Berkeley. BAIR operates the Open Research Commons (ORC) which brings together academia and industry to cultivate an open, interdisciplinary research environment.

1110.notes: The Berkeley Institute for Data Science (BIDS) is a central hub of data-intensive research, open source software, and data science training programs at UC Berkeley that launched in 2013. BIDS is an integral part of UC Berkeley's College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS) and was made possible by grants from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation and the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation. The Institute is one of three Moore-Sloan Data Science Environments along with data science organizations at the University of Washington and New York University. BIDS is currently led by Fernando Pérez as Faculty Director.

1111.notes: Multiple organizations operate under the name "Responsible AI Initiative" with different scopes and affiliations. The University of Utah operates the One-U Responsible AI Initiative, which aims to advance AI to achieve societal good while protecting privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties. Emory University launched a Responsible AI website as part of their enterprise-wide Responsible AI initiative, led by the Emory AI Group with input from the Responsible AI Executive Governance Committee. Carnegie Mellon University launched a Responsible AI initiative out of the Block Center for Technology and Society with support from faculty in the School of Computer Science.
