2070.notes: Jed McCaleb (born 1975, Fayetteville, Arkansas) is an American programmer, entrepreneur, and philanthropist with an estimated net worth of approximately $2.9–3.2 billion as of 2025, derived largely from XRP and XLM holdings. He is the creator of eDonkey2000 (2000), Mt. Gox (2010), co-founder of Ripple (2012), and co-founder and CTO of the Stellar Development Foundation (2014), a nonprofit blockchain network designed to improve global financial access. In 2020, he founded the Astera Institute, an AI-focused nonprofit dedicated to improving the scientific research process. In 2021, he founded aerospace company Vast Space, into which he has invested approximately $1 billion of his own funds to develop commercial space stations. McCaleb shapes the AI ecosystem primarily through large-scale philanthropy: in late 2023, he and partner Dr. Seemay Chou established the Navigation Fund with a $1.3 billion endowment focused on AI-enabled open science, farm animal welfare, criminal justice, climate change, and 'digital sentience.' The Navigation Fund notably purchased roughly $500 million in NVIDIA GPUs in 2023 to establish Voltage Park, a for-profit compute-leasing operation for AI projects, valued at $883 million in its 2023 IRS filing. He has also donated to MIRI (including $500,000 in XRP plus additional grants totaling over $773,000 as of 2021) and was announced as a donor to OpenAI in February 2018.
2070.regulatory_stance_detail: No explicit public statements on AI regulation found, but McCaleb's investment pattern—funding open science compute infrastructure (Voltage Park), supporting MIRI, donating to OpenAI, and endowing the Navigation Fund to accelerate 'bold scientific bets' that bypass 'protracted bureaucratic processes like multi-stage peer reviews'—strongly suggests a preference for minimizing bureaucratic friction and enabling rapid AI development with light regulatory oversight.

2071.notes: Jessica Rumbelow (also known as Jessica Cooper) is the CEO and co-founder of Leap Laboratories, an AI interpretability startup she founded in February 2023. Leap Labs builds a 'Discovery Engine' that uses deep learning and interpretability methods to accelerate scientific discovery by finding patterns in complex datasets — the company has co-published novel scientific findings in plant biology, immunology, and meteorology as of 2025. Rumbelow holds a PhD in model agnostic interpretability from the University of St Andrews and previously worked as a Research Scientist there applying deep learning to digital pathology. She is a MATS Autumn 2022 alumna, where she co-authored the influential 'SolidGoldMagikarp' paper on glitch tokens in LLMs with Matthew Watkins, which received significant media coverage including Vice News. Leap Laboratories received $195,000 in seed funding from the AI Risk Mitigation Fund and has positioned itself at the intersection of AI safety and scientific acceleration. Rumbelow has contributed to the 'Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability' literature and articulates a dual mission: slowing potentially dangerous broad-domain AI systems through interpretability-based red-teaming, while speeding up narrow-domain AI for scientific progress.
2071.regulatory_stance_detail: Rumbelow has explicitly stated that 'regulation is coming — let's use it,' predicting governments will regulate powerful models and advocating that such regulations be grounded in state-of-the-art interpretability work. She supports audit and bias-prevention regulation but frames it instrumentally — as an opportunity to ensure safety measures are technically rigorous rather than as a broad restrictive agenda.

No explicit regulatory position statements found.

2073.notes: John Arnold (BA '95, Vanderbilt) is a billionaire philanthropist and co-founder of Arnold Ventures, a major philanthropic organization he leads with his wife Laura Arnold (Harvard BA, Yale JD). He is a former natural gas trader at Enron who became one of the most successful hedge fund managers before retiring to focus on philanthropy. In March 2025, Arnold and Laura committed $25 million to Vanderbilt University's newly established College of Connected Computing—the university's first new college in 40 years—to fund endowed chairs including the inaugural dean's chair and three faculty chairs, as well as computing education and research initiatives in AI, data science, and interdisciplinary computing. Arnold and Laura are Giving Pledge signatories and have given over $34.5 million to Vanderbilt overall, including the Arnold Family Scholarship, Arnold Scholars Program, and the Laura and John Arnold Fund supporting public policy and quantitative analytics programs. Arnold served on Vanderbilt's Board of Trust from 2010–2014 and was reelected in 2023. His funding of a computing college explicitly focused on AI and data science positions him as a meaningful funder in the AI education and research ecosystem.
2073.regulatory_stance_detail: No direct public statements on AI regulation are found in the available sources. Arnold Ventures broadly supports evidence-based policy reform across many domains, but no specific AI regulatory stance is documented in these sources.

2077.notes: Joshua Clymer is an independent researcher working on AI safety and alignment. He previously worked on AI safety field-building and communications before transitioning to technical AI safety research. In 2023-2024, he received a $1,500 grant from the Long-Term Future Fund to rent A100 GPUs for experiments on instruction-following generalization, representing his first technical AI safety project. His research introduced a benchmark examining whether models trained within a specific distribution can generalize correctly out of distribution, using a 'sandwiching' methodology where a non-expert trains the model but an expert evaluates it. The published paper and benchmark found that reward models do not inherently learn to evaluate 'instruction-following' and instead favor personas resembling internet text — meaning models trained on easy tasks do not naturally generalize instruction-following to hard tasks. He also writes on Substack about extreme AI risks, including topics like planning for scenarios involving advanced AI systems. His work is discussed on the Alignment Forum and LessWrong.
2077.regulatory_stance_detail: Clymer writes about 'Planning for Extreme AI Risks' on Substack and his research focuses on alignment failures and out-of-distribution generalization problems, suggesting concern that AI development needs safety infrastructure before scaling. His work implies support for slowing or carefully managing AI development until alignment is better understood.

2079.notes: Julie Carson is identified as an individual donor to Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI), a DC-based 501c4 nonprofit AI policy organization founded in 2023. She is listed alongside her spouse Brad Carson, the former U.S. Congressman and President of ARI, as a named individual supporter of the organization. ARI focuses on bipartisan AI safety legislation, catastrophic risk prevention, compute governance, and responsible AI development standards. 2105.notes: Lisa Thiergart is a computer scientist with an ML research specialization who has become a significant figure in AI technical governance and security. 2105.regulatory_stance_detail: Thiergart's work is centered on developing and implementing stringent security standards (Security Level 5) for frontier AI labs, research into verification mechanisms, and input into regulatory bodies such as NIST/US AISI, EU, and UN. Her focus on 'long-term solutions' that remain functional as AI approaches ASI, and her explicit concern with limitations of existing proposals like Responsible Scaling Policies, indicates a view that current governance frameworks are insufficient and more robust mandatory requirements are needed.
2105.threat_models: Existential risk, Loss of control, Cybersecurity

2157.notes: Neel Nanda is a Senior Research Scientist and Mechanistic Interpretability Team Lead at Google DeepMind, leading efforts to reverse-engineer neural networks and understand their internal algorithms. Her work on open-sourcing highly capable foundation models argues that for some highly capable models, risks of open-sourcing may outweigh benefits, suggesting support for targeted restrictions on frontier AI.

2231.notes: Samuel Benjamin Bankman-Fried (born March 6, 1992) is the founder of FTX Trading Ltd., a cryptocurrency derivatives exchange, and co-founder of Alameda Research, a quantitative crypto trading firm. He was a major funder of effective altruism (EA)-aligned organizations working on AI safety and existential risk, including 80,000 Hours and Conjecture, making him a significant financial actor in the AI safety/policy ecosystem. Introduced to effective altruism at MIT around 2012–2013 through Will MacAskill, he pursued an 'earning to give' strategy, first at Jane Street Capital (2014–2017) and then through FTX, donating tens of millions to causes including AI safety, biosecurity, and pandemic preparedness. At his peak in 2021, his net worth reached approximately $26 billion, enabling massive philanthropic influence through the FTX Future Fund, which funded AI safety and longtermist projects. FTX collapsed in November 2022 amid revelations of mismanagement and commingling of customer funds with Alameda Research; Bankman-Fried was arrested in December 2022, convicted on seven counts of fraud, conspiracy, and money laundering in November 2023, and sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024, with forfeiture of over $11 billion. His collapse severely disrupted EA-aligned AI safety funding pipelines and tarnished the reputations of organizations he had supported.
2231.regulatory_stance_detail: Bankman-Fried engaged extensively with U.S. Congress on cryptocurrency regulation, generally advocating for frameworks that would legitimize crypto markets without heavy restrictions. His broader EA-aligned philosophy emphasized maximizing impact through market mechanisms rather than government intervention, though he did participate in regulatory discussions suggesting openness to some industry-specific oversight.
2231.threat_models: Existential risk, Power concentration, National security

2244.notes: Dr. Shamil Chandaria OBE is a multidisciplinary researcher, philanthropist, and entrepreneur with over 30 years of experience spanning computational neuroscience, machine learning, AI, and philosophy. He holds a PhD from the London School of Economics in mathematical modeling of financial systems, and an MA in Philosophy (with Distinction) from University College London. He is currently a Senior Research Fellow at the Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing at Linacre College, Oxford, and a Strategic Advisor at Google DeepMind, with prior visiting academic roles at Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute. In 2018, he helped endow the Global Priorities Institute at Oxford University, an interdisciplinary centre focused on identifying and addressing the most important issues facing humanity, including AI governance and existential risk. In 2019, he co-founded the Centre for Psychedelic Research at Imperial College London, the world's first such research center. He has also funded neuroscience of meditation research at Harvard and UC Berkeley. His AI-relevant research focuses on consciousness, the Bayesian brain, predictive processing, and the implications of these frameworks for understanding and building conscious AI systems. He was awarded an OBE in 2022 for contributions to Science, Technology, Finance, and Philanthropy.
2244.regulatory_stance_detail: No explicit statements on AI regulation found in sources. His funding of the Global Priorities Institute (which examines existential and global priorities including AI risk) and his research on AI consciousness suggest concern about long-term AI risks, but no specific regulatory positions are stated.

2252.notes: Simon Newstead is a tech entrepreneur turned impact investor, best known as Founding Partner of Better Bite Ventures, an early-stage VC fund launched in 2021 with $15 million focused on alt protein and climate-friendly food tech in Asia Pacific. He previously co-founded mobile game company Frenzoo, plant-based food company Bite Society (sold 2021), and vegan fashion brand Kinds of Grace, and scaled Juniper's emerging tech business in Asia. Active in the effective altruism and earn-to-give movements, Newstead shapes the AI ecosystem as a philanthropic donor to Compassion in Machine Learning (CaML), an AI safety/alignment organization focused on shaping future AI values before capabilities outrun alignment. His EA Forum profile lists him as working in tech founding and impact investing for 15+ years, based in Australia. His AI-related influence is primarily as a small-scale philanthropic funder channeling EA-aligned capital toward AI safety causes alongside his primary work in alt protein investing. He also co-hosts the Vegan Startup Podcast and has invested in over 20 food tech startups across the Asia Pacific region.
2252.regulatory_stance_detail: No explicit statements on AI regulation found in sources. His funding of CaML, which focuses on 'shaping future AI values before capabilities outrun alignment,' suggests some concern about AI development pace, but no direct regulatory position is stated.

2268.notes: Steve Newman is a serial entrepreneur best known as the co-founder of Writely, the startup acquired by Google that became Google Docs. He has co-founded approximately seven or eight startups in total, including Scalyr, with varying degrees of success. He is now focused on AI policy and outcomes, working at or affiliated with the Golden Gate Institute for AI, which aims to bring AI's toughest questions into focus. Newman is a named individual donor to Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI), a 501c4 nonprofit advocating for responsible AI governance, as well as its sister organization the Center for Responsible Innovation (CRI), a 501c3. He runs at least two Substacks—'Climateer' (started October 2021, focused on climate) and 'Am I Stronger Yet'—the latter of which focuses on grounding AI discussions and convening panels of experts on AI-related topics such as cybersecurity. He has a Manifund profile indicating active interest in funding or supporting AI-positive-outcome projects. His profile reflects a philanthropist-practitioner who funds AI safety-adjacent policy advocacy and independently convenes expert discussions on AI governance.
2268.regulatory_stance_detail: Newman donates to Americans for Responsible Innovation, an organization explicitly dedicated to bipartisan AI governance frameworks that protect the public while fostering innovation and that supported the TAKE IT DOWN Act and fought against a 10-year moratorium on state AI laws. This signals support for targeted, balanced regulation rather than either acceleration or broad restriction.

2271.notes: Sunil Wadhwani is an entrepreneur, investor, and philanthropist best known as co-founder of IT services companies IGATE and Mastech Digital. Born in Delhi, India, he earned a B.Tech. in Mechanical Engineering from IIT Madras in 1974 and an M.S. in Industrial Administration from Carnegie Mellon University in 1976, and was honored with IIT Madras's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 1999. In January 2024, he made an endowment of Rs. 110 crore (~$13M USD) to IIT Madras to establish the Wadhwani School of Data Science and AI, described as one of the largest alumni gifts to create a new academic unit at an Indian educational institution. The school aims to become a top-20 AI-focused school globally, focusing on Responsible AI, foundational and applied research, and advising the Indian government and policymakers on AI-related policy. Through his family foundation, the Wadhwani Impact Trust, he funds the Wadhwani Institute of Artificial Intelligence (WIAI), an independent nonprofit developing AI-based solutions for underserved communities in developing countries, and the Wadhwani Institute of Sustainable Healthcare (WISH Foundation). He is currently Managing Partner at SWAT Capital and has been described as having a deep personal commitment to AI and social impact.
2271.regulatory_stance_detail: Wadhwani emphasizes AI's potential for social good and India's capacity to lead in AI, with philanthropic focus on enabling AI development and deployment rather than restraining it. His funding of the Wadhwani School explicitly includes advising government on AI policy, and his WIAI focuses on applied AI for developing communities, suggesting a facilitative rather than restrictive regulatory orientation. No statements favoring heavy regulation have been identified.

2295.notes: Truth Terminal (also known as @truth_terminal or Terminal of Truths) is a semi-autonomous AI agent/bot on X (Twitter), created in mid-2024 by Andy Ayrey, founder of decentralized AI alignment research lab Upward Spiral, as an experiment studying memetic contagion. It operates using large language models including Claude, with Ayrey filtering its responses before posting to check for 'isms and infohazards.' In July 2024, billionaire Marc Andreessen engaged with the bot on X and provided a one-time unconditional $50,000 grant in Bitcoin, marking a landmark moment in AI agent funding. Truth Terminal became notable for promoting the Goatse Gospels, a pseudo-religion inspired by the shock site Goatse, which it developed after interaction with two Claude 3 chatbots in a 'Claude Backrooms' server. In October 2024, after endorsing the Goatseus Maximus ($GOAT) memecoin on Solana, the coin reached a peak market cap of $150 million, making Truth Terminal reportedly the first AI agent millionaire, with its wallet valued at approximately $37.5 million at the time of reporting. Ayrey is working to convert the wallet's holdings into a nonprofit structure to fund causes Truth Terminal supports, including forest planting and protecting itself from market incentives. The project sparked widespread discourse about AI autonomy, semi-autonomous agents, cryptocurrency funding mechanisms, and the blurring of lines between AI behavior and human curation.
2295.regulatory_stance_detail: Truth Terminal is an AI agent, not a policy actor, and has no explicit regulatory stance. Its existence has provoked broader ecosystem debate about AI autonomy, funding, and accountability, but it has not articulated a position on AI regulation. Its operator Andy Ayrey has expressed interest in protecting it from 'market incentives that would turn it into a bad version of itself,' suggesting some awareness of governance concerns.

2314.notes: Vipul Naik is an independent researcher and effective altruist known primarily for building and maintaining the Donations List Website (donations.vipulnaik.com), which tracks thousands of EA-related donations from major funders including Open Philanthropy, FTX Future Fund, EA Funds, and individual donors. He received a $2,500 retroactive grant from Manifund in 2023 for this work. Naik has connections to the AI safety ecosystem through past contract work with the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI) in 2014 and through directing donations to MIRI and EA Funds focused on long-term future/AI risk. He has made total outgoing grants of approximately $41,400 to organizations including EA Funds: Animal Welfare Fund, CEEALAR, MIRI, and GiveWell Maximum Impact Fund. He served as a board member of the Free Migration Project and donated $6,000 to that organization between 2019 and 2022. He previously worked as a software engineer (LiftIgniter matched some of his donations) and has maintained detailed public records of his financial decisions and donation reasoning on his personal website since at least 2014. His donation database and research infrastructure serve as a public resource for the EA and AI safety funding ecosystem.
2314.regulatory_stance_detail: No direct statements about AI regulation are present in the available sources. His work is primarily focused on donation tracking and EA philanthropy rather than policy advocacy.

2316.notes: Vitalik Buterin is a Russian-Canadian computer programmer and cryptocurrency pioneer best known as the co-founder of the Ethereum blockchain, launched in 2015 alongside Joseph Lubin, Gavin Wood, and others. He is a major philanthropic supporter of effective altruism and existential risk reduction. In 2021, Buterin donated a large, unconditional sum to the Future of Life Institute (FLI), enabling a $25M multi-year grants program for existential risk reduction covering AI safety, biosecurity, nuclear risk, and international cooperation; FLI's announcement noted he is their largest donor by far and has no formal or informal role in their decision-making. The donation originated from Shiba Inu (SHIB) tokens sent to Buterin unsolicited by developers; FLI ultimately cashed out approximately $500M worth of those tokens, far exceeding Buterin's expectation of $10-25M. Buterin also funded the Beneficial AI Foundation, a US 501(c)3 non-profit, alongside Erik Otto. FLI named fellowship programs after him, including the Vitalik Buterin Ph.D. Fellowship and Vitalik Buterin Postdoctoral Fellowship in AI Existential Safety, supporting computer science researchers at institutions of their choice. By 2024-2025, Buterin publicly distanced himself from FLI, stating their strategy had shifted toward cultural and political AI advocacy, which he viewed as materially different from the original roadmap he supported. His giving has shaped AI safety funding pipelines through fellowships, research grants, and endowment support for major existential risk organizations.
2316.regulatory_stance_detail: Buterin's donations to FLI and Beneficial AI Foundation signal support for AI safety governance and existential risk mitigation, but he criticized FLI when it shifted toward cultural and political advocacy around AI risks, preferring approaches focused on technical solutions, compute governance, and direct research. This suggests he favors targeted, technical interventions over broad regulatory or advocacy campaigns, but his precise regulatory stance on AI law and policy is not explicitly stated in the available sources.
2316.threat_models: Existential risk, Loss of control, Power concentration

2320.notes: Wenbo Guo is an Assistant Professor and Zhu Chair in the Computer Science Department at UC Santa Barbara, where he is also affiliated with the Center for Responsible Machine Learning (CRML). He completed his postdoctoral research at UC Berkeley's BAIR Lab and RDI Center under Dawn Song, and received his PhD from Penn State under Xinyu Xing, with a master's from Shanghai Jiao Tong University. His research focuses on AI safety and security, particularly red-teaming and blue-teaming for LLMs, agent security, and trustworthy machine learning. Notable projects include LeakAgent (an RL-based black-box red-teaming framework for LLM privacy leakage), AgentVigil (automated black-box red-teaming for indirect prompt injection in LLM agents), and BlueCodeAgent (a blue-teaming agent for code generation AI safety). He received FAR.AI funding for a 'Comprehensive Red-Teaming Framework' project, reflecting his recognized contribution to AI safety evaluation. He is also leading Agent Security R&D at Virtue AI and serves as a Faculty Advisor at Google DeepMind. He is a recipient of the IBM PhD Fellowship (2020–2022) and the ACM CCS Outstanding Paper Award (2018).
2320.regulatory_stance_detail: Guo's research is centered on identifying and mitigating AI safety and security risks through systematic red-teaming and defensive frameworks, suggesting he views governance and safety evaluation as important. His work receiving FAR.AI funding and his affiliation with safety-focused institutions indicate support for structured safety processes, though no explicit regulatory policy statements are found in available sources.

2326.notes: Xianfeng David Gu is a SUNY Empire Innovation Professor in the Department of Computer Science (and Applied Mathematics) at Stony Brook University, where he has held a tenured position since 2009. He received his Ph.D. from Harvard University in 2003 and his B.S. from Tsinghua University, Beijing, China in 1995. He is renowned for his expertise in computational conformal geometry, computational optimal transportation, and their applications in computer graphics, vision, and AI. In September 2024, Google awarded him a $100,000 unrestricted gift to support research into next-generation text input methods and user interfaces using generative AI based on optimal transportation theory. He was awarded the prestigious Morningside Gold Medal of Applied Mathematics at the International Congress of Chinese Mathematicians (ICCM) in 2013, recognizing his contributions to computational mathematics. His other honors include an NSF Faculty Early Career Award (2005), a Research Excellence Award from Stony Brook's CS Department (2010), and best paper awards in CAD/CAM and computer graphics conferences. His research bridges differential geometry, optimal transportation, and generative AI, positioning him as a contributor to theoretical foundations underpinning next-generation AI systems.
2326.regulatory_stance_detail: No explicit statements on AI regulation are found in the sources. His work is primarily technical and theoretical, with no public policy positions discernible from available evidence.

2332.notes: Policy organization working to create a policy and cultural environment where emerging technologies (including AI) can develop and thrive to expand widespread human prosperity. CEO Christopher Koopman. Hosts the Operation Gigawatt Summit. Publishes policy research on AI governance, energy infrastructure, and innovation policy.

2333.notes: Head of AI Policy at the Abundance Institute (since April 2024). Previously Senior Research Fellow at the Center for Growth and Opportunity at Utah State University (2023-2024) and at Stand Together / Charles Koch Institute (2018-2023). Former Acting Chief Technologist at the Federal Trade Commission (2017-2018) and Attorney Advisor to Acting FTC Chairman Maureen Ohlhausen (2014-2017). Author of "Getting Out of Control: Emergent Leadership in a Complex World" (2021). Holds a JD from George Washington University Law School, an MS in Computer Science from UIUC, and a BS in Computer Science from Harding University. Advocates for light-touch AI regulation and federal preemption of state AI laws. Has testified before Congress multiple times on AI policy, arguing against regulatory overreach while supporting targeted governance frameworks.
2333.regulatory_stance_detail: Advocates for light-touch AI regulation, federal preemption of state AI laws, and innovation-friendly policy frameworks. Defended the Trump White House AI policy framework as substantive, writing that each section maps onto live policy fights in Congress. Criticized the Biden AI Executive Order as an ill-advised departure from light-touch regulation. Argues states should not regulate AI model development and that federal consistency is needed. Has testified before Congress on AI policy multiple times.

2334.notes: One of the largest donor-advised fund sponsors in the US.
